podcast.title: Marriage to Phil Spector (1968)
podcast.body: Following the breakup of The Ronettes in 1967, Ronnie married Phil Spector in 1968, a union that was characterized by his increasingly controlling and abusive behavior towards her. "the next year running married Phil Spectre, who became ever more controlling and abusive."

podcast.title: Escape from Abusive Marriage (June 1972)
podcast.body: Ronnie finally managed to escape her abusive marriage to Phil Spector in June 1972, leaving their home barefoot after he had stolen her shoes to prevent her departure. She faced a long struggle with alcoholism in the years that followed. "Ronnie eventually escaped from Spectre's abuse, leaving the house barefoot, as Spectre had stolen her shoes so she couldn't leave, and started to build a new life for herself, though she would struggle with alcoholism for many years."

podcast.title: John Lennon and Jimmy Iovine's Help
podcast.body: Her solo career gained significant momentum after a chance meeting in New York where her old friend John Lennon introduced her to producer Jimmy Iovine. Iovine, then producing an album for Southside Johnny and the Asbury Jukes, suggested Ronnie sing a duet on a Bruce Springsteen-written song for the band, which she recorded that day. "Her old friend John Lennon saw her on the street and called her over for a chat, and introduced her to the friend he was with, Jimmy Iovine..."

podcast.title: Life Story Film Announced (September last year)
podcast.body: In September of the previous year (relative to the podcast's release), a film about Ronnie Spector's life story was announced, intended to portray her as the central protagonist rather than a secondary character in the narrative of her abusive husband. "In September last year, it was announced that a film is going to be made of Rani's Specter's life story."

podcast.title: No Financial Settlement from Divorce
podcast.body: In her divorce from Phil Spector, Ronnie received no financial settlement. Spector explicitly threatened to hire a hitman to kill her if she pursued any claims against him, forcing her to make a living by touring the nostalgia circuit with new lineups of "Ron Eats" (Ronettes). "She got nothing in that of her settlement, as Spectre threatened to hire a hitman to kill her if she tried to get anything from him..."

podcast.title: Solo Version of "Don't Worry Baby" (Decades Later)
podcast.body: Many decades after its original release, Ronnie Spector recorded a solo rendition of "Don't Worry Baby." While acknowledged as a "fine performance," the recording is noted to "miss something" when sung by a woman rather than a man, due to the song's intrinsic focus on male insecurity relating to "toxic masculinity." "Rani Spectre recorded a solo version of it many decades later, and it's a fine performance, but the limit misses something when it's sung by a woman rather than a man."
